summary: Yasuhiro Okazaki is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He completed his PhD at Hiroshima University under Atsushi Uno, Shoryu Katsura, and Hiroakira Ono, and held posts at Chiyoda, Hiroshima Prefectural Kabe, and Hiroshima Prefectural Takamiya high schools (attested 2005).

Yasuhiro Sueki is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He undertook short-term study under George Baumann at Tübingen University Library and held posts at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~1982–1996) and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996).

Yasuhiro Tsuchiyama is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He has served as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yasuhiro Ueno works in Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2003–2004), where he also held a post, and served as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University (attested 2004).

Yasuhiro Yamazaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Koyasan University (~1950–1954). He served as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University (1966–2000) and as a professor at Koyasan University (~1974–2000).

Yasuke Ikari is an Indologist who studied at Kyoto University and earned a PhD from the University of Chicago (~1969–1973). He held posts at Kindai University, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Kyoto University, becoming professor emeritus in 2004.

Yasuko Kojima is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics. She has held lecturer posts at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Yasumasa Sekine is a religious studies and Indology scholar who studied at Tokyo Institute of Technology and SOAS. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology, Gakushuin Women's Junior College, University of Tsukuba, Japan Women's University, and Kwansei Gakuin University.

Yasunori Ejima was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who earned his degrees at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia, Nagaoka University of Technology, and the University of Tokyo.

Yasuo Deguchi is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University. He taught at Nagoya Institute of Technology before returning to Kyoto University, where he became a professor and dean, later visiting ZEN University in 2025.
Yasuo Goto is a Buddhist studies scholar who held lecturer posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1991 and 2006) and served as a part-time lecturer at Shuchiin University (attested 2006).
Yasuo Inamoto is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a technical official at Nara National Museum (~1995–2004) before taking up a post at Kyoto University in ~2004.

Yasuo Matsunami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1992–2006) and as an advisor to the Śrāvakabhūmi Study Group.
Yasuo Sano is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyu Mitomo (attested 1996) and founded the Buha Bukkyo Shiso Kenkyukai.

Yasuo Yuasa was a philosophy and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji. He held faculty posts at the University of Yamanashi, Osaka University, and the University of Tsukuba.

Yasuro Abe is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Wako and Otani universities. He held posts at Osaka, Otemae, and Nagoya universities, later joining Ryukoku University in 2019.

Yasusaburo Sakaki was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1895–1899), where he later held a post (~1899–1906), before serving at Kyushu University (~1906–1929).

Yasushi Endo is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Nagoya University, as a professor at Shitennoji University (attested 2000), and as a full-time lecturer at Aichi Bunkyo University (attested 2000–2004).

Yasutaka Muroya is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He worked as a project research associate at the University of Vienna and the University of Leipzig, and as a research associate at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1963–1971). He held posts at Yamaguchi University (~1974–1999) and Koyasan University (~1999–2006), and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies.
